coverage_kind_FD001.source: models/results_phase5b.json mc_dropout.FD001_post_hoc.note: FD001 test coverage had already been seen in Phase 5, so this is not a confirmation

value.RUL: Remaining useful life: cycles left before the engine fails. Training targets and test truth are capped at 125 cycles.
value.interval: MC-dropout 90% interval with rule E scale factors (models/calibration_rule.json): mean +/- k x sd over 100 dropout passes, k switched on predicted RUL <= 50.
value.near_failure: Test engines whose true RUL <= 50 cycles.
value.RMSE: Root mean squared error of predicted vs true (capped) RUL over the 100 test engines of a dataset, in cycles.
value.near_failure_MAE: Mean absolute error over near-failure test engines, in cycles.
value.coverage: Share of test engines whose true capped RUL lies inside the 90% interval.
value.OEE: Availability x Performance x Quality from summed hours and units (maintenance/simulate.py oee()). Availability = run hours / planned hours; Performance = actual units / ideal units; Quality = good units / actual units. SIMULATED plant: not measured data.
value.drift_false_alarm_rate: Phase 7 rule v1: share of clean test runs with a drift test in which at least one sensor was flagged drifted.
value.clean_run_flag_rate: Phase 7b rule v2: share of clean replay runs with needs_retraining set (criterion C1, limit 5%, pipeline/phase7b_criteria.json).
value.shift: One flow run per dataset per 8-hour shift = one engine cycle.

value.renewal: A service or a repair ends the machine's current engine life (the engine is replaced or overhauled to new). OEE is totalled over each machine's single life; by the renewal-reward theorem the fleet ratio equals the long-run ratio if lives repeat.
value.calendar: All machines start at cycle 1 on day 0 and run CYCLES_PER_DAY cycles a day (the Phase 2 replay convention). A machine fails when it completes cycle L (its true failure point, RUL 0). It runs degraded (speed loss, more scrap) in its last 20 cycles, i.e. while its TRUE remaining life is < 20.
value.service_timing: A service booked for day d happens at the start of day d, before that day's cycles run.
value.after_data_ends: NASA test files stop before failure. After a machine's last reading the predictive policy has no new data, so it keeps using its last forecast, aged by one cycle per cycle run.
value.crew_limit: Only the predictive policy is crew-limited (as in the guide). Run-to-failure and fixed-interval services are not, which favours the two baselines.
value.work_orders: A booked service is kept (no re-planning of booked orders). An engine with an open order is not re-booked. If it fails before its service day, that is an unplanned failure and the order is cancelled. Flagged engines left unserved are retried the next day.
value.rounding: rul_low is floored to whole cycles before scheduling (the guide's int()); flooring is conservative.

published_rule.value: LSTM replaces XGBoost only if H1 is significant after Holm with LSTM better AND its pooled near-failure MAE is not worse

simulation_notice.value: SIMULATED plant: production, downtime and OEE are not measured data
